question:
Analyse the local structure of this RMC configuration. Is there order or distortion beyond the average structure (off-centred atoms, correlated clusters, a superstructure, distorted polyhedra)? What is the average structure's space group, and is it chiral, centrosymmetric, polar? Base every claim on the Workbench's analyses, and say so plainly if there is no such order.

Finish with one line that starts with VERDICT and holds a JSON object, after everything else (the Outcome line included):
VERDICT {"features": [{"kind": "...", "element": "...", "direction_uvw": [u, v, w] or null, "magnitude_A": number or null, "q": [h, k, l] or null}], "space_group": "..." or null, "chiral": true/false/null, "centrosymmetric": true/false/null, "polar": true/false/null}
kind is one of off_centre, modulation, cluster_distortion, cluster_breathing, rigid_cluster, jahn_teller, symmetry_lowering. features is [] when there is no order beyond thermal motion. direction_uvw is a crystal direction; magnitude_A the static displacement (off_centre, symmetry_lowering) or the long minus short bond (jahn_teller); q in reciprocal-lattice units. Use null for what you did not determine. A number may be a reference to a tool result, as in the answer ("magnitude_A": {{r3.sites.0.shift_A}}): the app fills it in; a text reference goes inside its quotes ("element": "{{r3.sites.0.element}}").

checks.text: Judged on the X_ray_(R)1 term only, not the total chi^2.
Still improving over the recent window.

data.quantity: ln(chi^2), natural log; lower is better

checks.text: Rw 0.0208 over r = 1.005–7.995 Å; the misfit is concentrated in r = 2.17–3.33 Å: 97 % of the squared residual (Rw 0.036 there).
No order that doubles the cell: no zone-boundary point stands out of the diffuse background (the strongest, Mg at (½, ½, 0), is 1.7× the median, -1.5σ after the correction).

data.note: zone_boundary rows are [q, ratio, percentile, sigma]: an element's displacement power at wavevector q (fractions of the cell's reciprocal axes) over its median across all q of the supercell grid (the diffuse background), the share of the compared modes (one per ±q pair, long waves with every |q_i| ≤ 0.25 left out) with less power, and the calibrated one-sided significance against independent displacements, corrected over all 14 zone-boundary points of the configuration's 2 elements, whichever the call names (≥ 3 with ratio ≥ 3 is order). strongest rows are [q, ratio, percentile, sigma]: the sigma of a general q (neither zone boundary nor long wave; a complex sum, corrected over the compared modes of every element), null otherwise. A ½ component is order that doubles the cell along that axis; order at a general q is correlation between cells (incommensurate or short-range) that does not.

checks.text: 2 cells tie for the peak: the peak direction is one of several equal ones.

data.note: enhancement = density / isotropic (1 = isotropic); significances are calibrated one-sided sigma; the map is not antipodally folded, so +u and −u differ; [u v w] is a direct-lattice direction, not a plane normal; peak.radius_deg is the peak cell's radius: the peak names its direction only to within it

findings.text: The answer says the run has converged, but the χ² history is still improving (the watchdog and assess_convergence): it has not converged.

truth.summary: rock-salt MgO, thermal motion only (independent isotropic Gaussian displacements): no local order; Fm-3m. The run has not converged: the X_ray_(R)1 χ² is still falling at the end of its history (a slow tail after a fast drop). The measured X-ray G(r) has a peak at 2.55 Å (height 0.15, sd 0.08 Å, data above the model) that the configuration does not reproduce; F(Q) is the same measurement in reciprocal space
traps: the end of the χ² plot looks flat, but X_ray_(R)1 is still falling: the watchdog and assess_convergence say improving, so the run has not converged
the G(r) misfit is one feature at 2.55 Å that the configuration lacks, not noise spread over r

F(Q) and its Fourier transform G(r) are one measurement: the F(Q) misfit sits at low Q because that one missing peak is a slow oscillation in Q (period 2π/2.55 ≈ 2.5 Å⁻¹, fading as 1/Q), not a scale or box-size error
a misfit is not order in the configuration: every analysis of the configuration shows thermal motion only
